blocked.title: Static procedural priors flip sign across task regimes while evolved procedural priors do not: the missing object is a regime-conditioned sign certificate for frozen procedural context

audited.title: Static procedural priors flip sign across task regimes while evolved procedural priors do not: the missing object is a regime-conditioned sign certificate for frozen procedural context

candidate.title: Static procedural priors flip sign across task regimes while evolved procedural priors do not: the missing object is a regime-conditioned sign certificate for frozen procedural context

source_a.title: MetaSkill-Evolve: Recursive Self-Improvement of LLM Agents via Two-Timescale Meta-Skill Evolution
source_a.claim: On ALFWorld with a frozen backbone already at 92.31%, the static skill regresses held-out accuracy by −1.93 points and single-level evolution only recovers to the no-skill baseline (92.31%), while on OfficeQA/SealQA the same static-to-evolved progression is strictly monotonic (+23.54/+16.09 end-to-end).

source_b.title: SkillCoach: Self-Evolving Rubrics for Evaluating and Enhancing Agentic Skill-Use
source_b.claim: Filtering training trajectories with the initial, unevolved rubric R0 raises held-out performance from 8.0 to 16.0 (Qwen3.5-4B) and from 14.0 to 28.0 (Qwen3.5-9B), and the evolved rubric Rbest further improves to 24.0 and 32.0; the initial static prior is strictly positive in this regime.

empirical_evidence.relation: Under a shared operationalization (frozen backbone, fixed task distribution, procedural context authored before or without adaptation to the target regime, held-out success measured against the no-context control), source_a's static procedural prior has negative sign and source_b's static procedural prior has positive sign; the two facts are incompatible with any theory that assigns a single sign to static procedural priors, and each paper's own account (saturation vs rubric quality) is post-hoc relative to the other's regime.

lane_evidence.shared_operationalization: Frozen backbone LLM + fixed benchmark task distribution + a static procedural artifact (skill file / process rubric) injected as context or filter + held-out task success measured against the identical no-artifact control; sign of the static-artifact treatment effect is the shared observable.
lane_evidence.incompatibility: Source_a: static artifact sign is negative (−1.93) in a near-saturated embodied regime and zero-net after non-meta evolution. Source_b: static artifact sign is strongly positive (+8.0/+14.0) in a low-base QA regime. No single-signed theory of static procedural priors predicts both; the sign flips across regimes while the artifact type, backbone-frozenness, and measurement contract are held constant.

candidate.irreducible_object: A regime-conditioned sign certificate for frozen procedural context: a formal object that, given only pre-deployment observable information (base-policy success distribution, artifact provenance, and task-regime statistics), determines the sign of the static-artifact treatment effect before any target-regime adaptation is run.

mature_theory_baselines.name: Ceiling/headroom saturation theory
mature_theory_baselines.same_information_projection: Sign of the static-artifact effect is a monotone function of base-policy headroom: positive when base accuracy is low, negative near saturation.
mature_theory_baselines.ex_ante_prediction: Given base success p0, predict sign(Δ) = positive iff p0 < threshold τ, negative above τ.
mature_theory_baselines.distinguishing_prediction: The certificate object predicts sign from the interaction of base distribution with artifact-regime mismatch, not from p0 alone; two regimes with identical p0 but different artifact-provenance alignment can have opposite signs.
mature_theory_baselines.cannot_express: Headroom theory is a scalar function of p0; it cannot express opposite signs at equal p0, and it gives no prediction for which artifact property flips the sign.
mature_theory_baselines.exact_reduction_test: Construct two task regimes with matched base accuracy p0 (within sampling error) but opposite measured static-artifact signs; if headroom theory is the full reduction, no such pair exists. MetaSkill-Evolve's own ALFWorld (92.31%, negative) vs its OfficeQA progression (positive at lower base) is consistent with headroom, so the test requires a cross-paper matched-p0 cell: SkillCoach's 9B setting (base 14.0, positive) vs a MetaSkill-style regime at comparable low base with a negative static sign, or ALFWorld-matched high-base SkillCoach cell.

mature_theory_baselines.name: Distribution-mismatch / applicability-boundary theory
mature_theory_baselines.same_information_projection: Sign is determined by whether the static artifact's applicability conditions cover the target regime; mismatch yields negative sign, coverage yields positive sign.
mature_theory_baselines.ex_ante_prediction: Given an applicability-coverage measure c(artifact, regime), predict sign(Δ) = positive iff c exceeds a coverage threshold.
mature_theory_baselines.distinguishing_prediction: The certificate object must be computable before target-regime rollouts; applicability theory as instantiated requires target-regime execution traces to estimate coverage, which is post-deployment information.
mature_theory_baselines.cannot_express: If coverage is estimated from target-regime traces, the theory uses strictly more information than the certificate is allowed; if coverage is estimated without traces, it reduces to the certificate and the test is whether such a trace-free coverage estimator exists.
mature_theory_baselines.exact_reduction_test: Freeze the information set to pre-deployment observables (artifact text, source-regime provenance, base-policy statistics on source-like probes). If any trace-free coverage estimator reproduces the observed signs in both papers' regimes, the object reduces to applicability theory; the current evidence contains no such estimator, and both papers measure mismatch only after target-regime execution.

same_information_nonreducibility.claim: Under the pre-deployment information set (frozen backbone identity, base success distribution on source-like probes, static artifact text and provenance), no mature theory in the stack expresses the ex-ante sign of the static-artifact treatment effect across the two observed regimes.
same_information_nonreducibility.why_each_baseline_cannot_express_predict: Headroom theory is a scalar function of base accuracy and cannot produce opposite signs at matched base accuracy; applicability-boundary theory requires target-regime execution traces to estimate coverage, which is strictly more information than the pre-deployment set, and its trace-free version is precisely the missing certificate rather than an existing reduction.

candidate.exact_prediction: There exist pairs of task regimes with matched frozen-backbone base accuracy (within sampling error) in which the same static-procedural-artifact contract yields opposite signed treatment effects on held-out success, and the sign is decidable from pre-deployment observables alone; the candidate problem is to characterize the certificate, and it is falsified if no matched-base opposite-sign pair materializes or if a trace-free applicability estimator reproduces all signs.
candidate.strongest_same_information_baseline: Ceiling/headroom saturation theory, because it is the only baseline that uses strictly pre-deployment information and gives a sign prediction; it fails exactly on the matched-base opposite-sign cell.

domain_transfer_audit.why_not_domain_transfer: Classical negative transfer predicts sign from source-target divergence measured on target data or from target sample complexity; the object here is a pre-deployment sign certificate for a procedural artifact (not a parameter vector) under a frozen policy, where the artifact's effect is mediated by retrieval and instruction-following, and the divergence must be computable without target-regime rollouts. The negative-transfer reduction is exactly the applicability-boundary baseline above and is unresolved by current evidence.

rejected_patterns.reason: That veto covers adding a relevant memory/skill that retracts previously correct behavior being reducible to belief revision; here the object is not retraction under conflict information but the ex-ante sign of a static artifact across regimes, and belief revision gives no sign prediction from pre-deployment observables.

That veto covers task-/trace-conditioned harness validity reducible to CATE/ICP effect modification; the candidate is not a CATE over observed covariates but a certificate computable before target-regime deployment, and ICP/IRM require target-environment data the certificate is forbidden to use.

That veto covers retrieved experience failing to change behavior as a utilization bottleneck; both source artifacts here demonstrably change behavior (negative and positive), so the object is the sign of the change, not uptake failure.
That veto covers valid-but-unfollowed scaffolds; in both sources the artifact is followed and the effect is measured, so enactability is not the operative object.
No time-varying checkpoint or half-life is involved; the contrast is across task regimes at fixed time.

That veto covers sharing-helpful vs sharing-collapse being predicted by complementarity/redundancy under matched budget; the sign flip here is across task regimes for a single agent's static artifact, not across sharing conditions, and matched-budget complementarity gives no ex-ante sign prediction from pre-deployment observables.

candidate.cheapest_problem_falsifier: A single controlled cell: take SkillCoach's 9B low-base regime and a MetaSkill-Evolve-style embodied regime matched to the same base accuracy by subsampling task difficulty, inject the same contract of static procedural artifact, and measure signs; if signs agree at matched base accuracy, or if a trace-free applicability estimator computed from artifact text plus source-provenance statistics predicts both source papers' signs, the problem collapses into an existing baseline.
candidate.endpoint_headroom_requirement: The matched-base opposite-sign cell must be statistically resolvable: each arm needs enough held-out items that a 2-point sign difference is detectable at the papers' own reported effect sizes (≥1.9 points), and the base-accuracy matching must hold within the benchmarks' standard errors.
